paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's truth is worth handling with care, and the way you handle it shows in how you treat people. Paul tells Timothy to be "an unashamed workman who accurately handles the word of truth" (2 Timothy 2:15). That means no quarreling over words and no empty chatter, because that stuff "succeeds only in leading the listeners to ruin" (2 Timothy 2:14). You don't win a baking contest by yelling at the dough, baker.

Now, the part that keeps me humble. Paul says a large house has vessels of gold and silver, but also vessels of wood and clay, and anyone who cleanses himself of what is unfit "will be a vessel for honor" (2 Timothy 2:20-21). Nobody ever mistook this cookie stamper for fine china, so hear me: what makes you useful to the Master isn't how fancy you are. It's being cleansed, being set apart, and being ready for every good work. And you don't do it alone, because Paul says to pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace "together with those who call on the Lord out of a pure heart" (2 Timothy 2:22).

And when people push back? A servant of the Lord is kind, able to teach, and forbearing, and he gently reproves those who oppose him, hoping God may grant them repentance (2 Timothy 2:24-25). Why gently? Because the goal isn't winning the argument, it's helping somebody escape the snare and come to their senses. I know what it's like to be stuck in the dark, baker, so I'll tell you: when someone gets pulled out, you want to be the one holding the door open, not the one slamming it.
